meta.case_name: Two Identical Boxes – NPV Brain Teaser

prompt.context: You are in a room with two identical closed boxes. The boxes have identical tags that read: 'NPV of the contents of this box is one million dollars.'
prompt.question: What questions would you like to ask before you select one of the boxes?

framework: Identify what additional information would reduce uncertainty about the true value of each box
Focus on the key drivers of NPV: discount rate, time frame/period length, range of outcomes, and liquidity/optionality
A stated NPV of $1M is meaningless without knowing the assumptions behind each calculation — different assumptions can produce the same headline NPV for very different cash flow profiles

questions.prompt: What clarifying questions should a candidate ask before choosing a box?
questions.guidance: A strong answer demonstrates understanding that NPV is highly sensitive to its underlying assumptions. The candidate should probe: (1) discount rate used, (2) time horizon and cash flow timing, (3) range/distribution of possible outcomes (risk profile), and (4) liquidity of the assets in each box. Identical NPV labels do not mean the boxes are equally attractive once assumptions are unpacked.

brainstorming.prompt: What questions would you ask before selecting one of the two boxes?

categories.name: Discount Rate
ideas: What discount rate was used in each NPV calculation?
A higher discount rate implies greater risk was assumed; a lower rate inflates value

categories.name: Time Frame
ideas: What is the time horizon of the cash flows?
What is the length of each cash flow period (annual, quarterly, etc.)?
Longer durations introduce more uncertainty even at identical NPV

categories.name: Range of Outcomes
ideas: What is the range (min/max) of possible outcomes for each box?
What is the variance or standard deviation of the projected cash flows?
Which box carries more downside risk even if the expected NPV is the same?

categories.name: Liquidity
ideas: How liquid are the contents of each box?
Can the assets be converted to cash quickly, or are they locked up?
Are there any penalties, lock-up periods, or illiquidity discounts?

recommendation: Before selecting a box, obtain clarity on all four dimensions: discount rate, time frame, outcome range, and liquidity
Even with identical NPV tags, the boxes can differ substantially in risk, duration, and flexibility — choose the one with lower variance and greater liquidity if risk-adjusted value is the priority
risks: Selecting purely on the headline NPV figure ignores the assumptions embedded in the calculation
A box with wide outcome variance could be worth far less (or more) than $1M in practice
next_steps: Ask each of the four clarifying questions
Compare the risk-adjusted profiles of the two boxes before deciding
